clue.text: Basket, one to catch fish originally

indicators.note: says the fish comes first, at the start of the word, though the clue mentions it last

parts.note: the bass is a common sea fish
the Roman numeral for one
a net is what you use to catch something

explanation.surface: A fishing basket, once used for landing catches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' is not a first-letter signal here: it places the fish at the front, ahead of 'one to catch'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bassinet is a hooded wicker cradle for a baby, a kind of basket.

clue.text: How setter perhaps goes round India to find architectural feature

indicators.note: the bark is placed around the abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: the noise a dog such as an Irish setter makes, its bark written bow-wow

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter travels round India seeking interesting buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'setter' is not the crossword compiler but the dog breed; 'How setter perhaps' asks what sound it makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved bay projecting from a house wall, glazed all round, is a notable building element.

clue.text: Genuine cases of contrite remorse shown after offence

indicators.note: the outer letters follow the offence in the answer

parts.note: a sin is a moral offence

indicators.note: the cases of a word are its outside letters, first and last

explanation.surface: Real repentance shows in contrition and remorse after wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both describe feelings that are honestly meant, not faked.

clue.text: Trendy cliques which are loose between the sheets?

definitions.text: which are loose between the sheets?

parts.note: fashionable things are 'in'
a set is a social clique

explanation.surface: Fashionable groups who are promiscuous in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests sexual looseness; the sheets are really pages, and the loose items are extra leaves slipped into a book or magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Inserted leaflets or pages sit loose between the bound pages of a publication.

clue.text: Flying seaplane initially disrupts seaside walk

indicators.note: flying here means sent into disorder, so the letters are shuffled
takes just the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A seaplane coming in low disturbs people strolling on the promenade.
explanation.definitionFit: A promenade along a seafront, where people stroll beside the beach.

clue.text: Agent works after taking year off

indicators.note: taking the year off means removing its letter from the word for works

parts.note: a works is a factory

explanation.surface: An employee goes back to work after a gap year.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is someone who does business on behalf of another, such as an estate manager.

clue.text: One fellow climbing tree makes slip?

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
the elder is a small tree

explanation.surface: A man going up a tree loses his footing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, slip is a fielding position close behind the batsman, so a slip is an example of this player; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Slip is a cricket position, so the player standing there is one of the side's catchers.

clue.text: Gym backs wearing different attire following cold snap

indicators.note: the rest follows the letter for cold

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: the reversed gym letters are worn inside the rearranged attire
the letters of attire are made different, rearranged into RITATE
backs is a verb here, going backwards, so the gym letters turn round

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym

explanation.surface: A cold spell has gym-goers wearing different outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snap' looks like a cold spell, but it is a verb for crackling; 'backs' is a verb too, meaning goes backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To crepitate is to crackle or make a sharp popping sound, as a snapping fire does.

clue.text: Composition improved endlessly after a month

indicators.note: the trimmed word comes after the month

parts.note: Oct is the short form of October

indicators.note: both ends are cut off the word for improved

parts.note: to better something is to improve it, and improved can also mean better

explanation.surface: A piece of music got better, but never quite finished, after a month.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical work written for eight players or voices is a type of composition.

clue.text: White stick finally discarded

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for stick is thrown away

parts.note: a wand is a slender stick

explanation.surface: A blind person's white stick has been thrown away at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White stick' reads as a blind person's cane, but White is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a pale, colourless face looks white or pallid.

clue.text: Extra time is needed by loose-limbed people

indicators.note: the time letter is attached to the people, sitting after them

parts.note: supple means flexible and loose-limbed
men as a general word for people

explanation.surface: Gymnasts need extra time to warm up.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: an additional section or allowance added on top of the main thing.

clue.text: He maybe is great shakes around Nigeria's capital

indicators.note: the shaken letters go around the capital letter
the letters of 'is great' are shaken up
a word's capital is its first letter

explanation.surface: Some man is a great success around the Nigerian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is not a man but the chemical symbol for helium, an example of the answer, hence 'maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium is one of the noble gases, the unreactive elements in the periodic table.

clue.text: Daughter is not unknown to be genteel

parts.note: ain't is the colloquial contraction of is not
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A daughter isn't a stranger to good manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both describe refined, delicate and rather prim behaviour.

clue.text: Finished even fewer duties around houses

indicators.note: the housed letters turn around, read backwards
the two words house the letters inside them

explanation.surface: Someone ended with even fewer household chores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like homes but is the signal for letters held inside fewer duties.
explanation.definitionFit: A game that ends level, neither side winning, is said to have been tied.

clue.text: Spring issue turns up on day that's convenient

indicators.note: the day letter is put on after the rest

parts.note: a well is a spring of water

indicators.note: in a down clue the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: to emit is to issue

explanation.surface: A spring delivery turns up on a convenient day.
explanation.definitionFit: Something timely, done at the right moment, is opportune.

clue.text: We should seize opportunity in conflict? It's hard to say

indicators.note: the we-plus-opportunity group goes inside the word for conflict

parts.note: to jar is to clash, and a jar is a disagreement

indicators.note: we takes hold of the opportunity, wrapping around it

parts.note: taken as written
a break is a lucky opportunity

explanation.surface: A call to seize the chance in war, followed by a shrug.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays two ways: a word that is hard to pronounce, and a hard boiled sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A long tongue-twisting word is difficult to pronounce, and the same name is given to a very hard sweet.

clue.text: Enthralling European exploit for one stout yeoman

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the beer holds the other letters

parts.note: stout is one example of beer
a feat is a heroic exploit

explanation.surface: A sturdy yeoman performs a captivating European feat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' looks like an adjective for the yeoman, but it is the dark drink, an example of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tower of London's warders are formally Yeomen of the Guard, popularly known by this nickname.

clue.text: Press discussed poser, one who's much admired

indicators.note: discussed means spoken about, so the word for press is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to roll something is to press it flat
a model poses for artists or photographers

explanation.surface: Journalists talked about a model who is widely admired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like the newspapers but is a verb, roll; 'poser' is a person posing, not a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A person others look up to and copy as an example is an exemplar.

clue.text: My wife wants wake-up call round about noon

indicators.note: the turned bugle call goes about the noon letter
the bugle call is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: reveille is the military wake-up call

explanation.surface: A man's wife wants him woken around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is not a possessive but the exclamation of surprise; ELLIEVER is the reversed bugle call, with N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of astonishment, as in 'My, how you've grown!'

clue.text: Compete successfully with fast runner towards the end

parts.note: the emu is a flightless bird that runs fast
late means near the end of a period

explanation.surface: A fast runner closing in late manages to compete successfully.
explanation.definitionFit: To match or rival someone's achievement, often by imitating them, is to equal them.

clue.text: With curtailment in all, "in name only" put another way

definitions.text: With curtailment in all, "in name only" put another way

indicators.note: the shortened letters are arranged another way, an anagram
every one of the three words loses its tail, its last letter

parts.note: the quoted phrase supplies the fodder, cut to I, NAM and ONL

explanation.surface: A wordsmith's note on how to shorten and rephrase a quoted phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted phrase does double duty: shortened and rearranged it gives the answer, and saying it another way gives the meaning too.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominal head holds the title without the real power; that word expresses the quoted phrase differently.

clue.text: King's Head's going to close for nobleman

indicators.note: the head, its first letter, moves to the close, the end of the word

parts.note: King Lear, Shakespeare's tragic king

explanation.surface: The landlord of the King's Head pub is closing it for an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King's Head' reads as a pub name; it is Shakespeare's King Lear, whose first letter goes to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A British peer ranking below a marquess and above a viscount, a titled aristocrat.

clue.text: Tumbler of brandy's first imbibed by a European

indicators.note: the letter is drunk in, taken inside the European

parts.note: a Croat is a European from Croatia

indicators.note: only the opening letter of brandy is used

explanation.surface: A glass of brandy is drunk by a European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tumbler' suggests a glass to suit the brandy, but it is a person who performs somersaults.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnastic performer doing somersaults and handsprings is a tumbler.

clue.text: Ready to break news? A bit of nerve's required

indicators.note: the money breaks into the pair, splitting them apart

parts.note: N is new, so news, as a plural, is two of them
ready is slang for cash, and the euro is a currency

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to break bad news, and it takes some nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'news' is read as the plural of 'new', N, giving two Ns; 'ready' means ready money.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerve cell is one of the basic units making up nervous tissue.

clue.text: Confined in nick, sons honour tradition

indicators.note: the sons letter is held within the nick

parts.note: a nick is a small cut
S is the abbreviation for son or sons
the OM, Order of Merit, is a British honour

explanation.surface: Locked up in jail, sons respect their family's traditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nick' looks like British slang for prison, but it is a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: an established practice handed down within a community.

clue.text: Periodically they'll spread revolutionary message

indicators.note: periodically takes every other letter of the word
revolutionary means turning round, so the spread reads backwards

parts.note: marge is British shorthand for margarine, a spread for bread

explanation.surface: Every so often, militants circulate a revolutionary message.
explanation.definitionFit: A written message sent by wire and delivered on paper, now largely historical.

clue.text: Run dodgy trade in cars? On the contrary!

indicators.note: the clue says trade in cars, a container signal
reverses the container: the cars go inside the shuffled trade, not the other way
dodgy means unsound, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Minis are small British cars

explanation.surface: A shady second-hand car dealer is asked to manage something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary!' flips 'trade in cars': the cars go into the anagram ADTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to manage or be in charge of an organisation's affairs.

clue.text: Qualified teacher gets the sack

definitions.meaning: a ..., Bachelor of Education degree, qualifies a teacher
the sack is slang for where you sleep, as in hit the sack

explanation.surface: A newly qualified teacher is promptly fired.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bachelor of Education degree, and the place you sleep, slang for a mattress.

clue.text: Resort Lake District neighbours for starters?

definitions.text: Resort Lake District neighbours for starters?

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort, sort again, so the letters are rearranged
takes the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A holiday resort bordering the Lake District, starters suggested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday town noun but is the anagram signal, re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendal is a Cumbrian market town just outside the Lake District national park, a gateway for visitors.

clue.text: Woman replaces contents of parcel before delivery

indicators.note: the inner letters of parcel are swapped out for the woman

parts.note: Renata is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman swaps the contents of a parcel before it is delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' looks like the post, but it means childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: Antenatal: describing the period of pregnancy before a baby is born.
